title: Normalized comparisons under a locally weakly equivalent enriched functor
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. A locally Kan simplicial category and its mapping complexes have the meanings of [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure]. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an enriched functor between locally Kan simplicial categories such that $\mathcal A(x,y)\to\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $x,y$. Fix $x,y$ and a vertex $b\in\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)$. The normalized comparison space
$$\mathcal N_V(x,y;b)=\mathcal A(x,y)\times_{\mathcal B(Vx,Vy),\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal B(Vx,Vy))\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)}\{b\}$$
is a contractible Kan complex. Its points are enriched maps together with a specified comparison homotopy to $b$, rather than all maps with no normalization. For composable fixed vertices $b:Vx\to Vy$ and $b':Vy\to Vz$, enriched composition and composition of the comparison paths give comparison points over $b'b$; all compatible relative higher comparisons take place in these same contractible homotopy fibres. If $b$ is invertible up to enriched homotopy, every corresponding map $x\to y$ is invertible up to enriched homotopy. In particular, for a fixed enriched homotopy equivalence $f:x\to y$, the homotopy fibre of $\mathcal A(y,x)\xrightarrow{-\circ f}\mathcal A(x,x)$ over $1_x$ is contractible; its points give inverse maps with their normalized inverse homotopy, and a second inverse homotopy exists. This normalization retains the specified comparison homotopies and their higher parameters; it makes no claim that the unnormalized space of equivalences between the objects is contractible.

proof.text: For the fixed pair $(x,y)$, write $V_{x,y}:\mathcal A(x,y)\to\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)$ for the map on mapping complexes; it is a map of Kan complexes because $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are locally Kan. By the definition of the homotopy fibre in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], its homotopy fibre over $b$ is exactly the displayed simplicial set $\mathcal N_V(x,y;b)$, including all parameter simplices. Kan property: by [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] the projection $p:E=\mathcal A(x,y)\times_{\mathcal B(Vx,Vy),\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal B(Vx,Vy))\to\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)$ induced by $\operatorname{ev}_1$ is a Kan fibration and its strict fibre over $b$ is $\mathcal N_V(x,y;b)$. That fibre is the pullback of $p$ along $\Delta^0\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal B(Vx,Vy)$, so its map to $\Delta^0$ has the right lifting property against every horn inclusion (a horn in the fibre maps to $E$, a filler of $p$ over the constant simplex at $b$ lies in the fibre); thus $\mathcal N_V(x,y;b)$ is a Kan complex. Weak contractibility alone would not give this. Contractibility: the hypothesis says $V_{x,y}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, so [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] makes this homotopy fibre contractible; in particular it is nonempty and connected.

proof.text: Enriched composition is a simplicial map on the two mapping complexes. Applying it degreewise to a pair of paths $V(a)\leadsto b$ and $V(a')\leadsto b'$ gives a path $V(a'a)\leadsto b'b$; the endpoint identities use that $V$ preserves enriched composition. Because the construction is simplicial, it carries every higher parameter and every compatibility among the two comparison paths to the corresponding simplex in the normalized fibre over $b'b$.

source.place: HTT §2.2.3.11, enriched mapping-space composition and coherent comparison data

proof.text: Assume $b$ is invertible up to enriched homotopy: there are a vertex $\bar b\in\mathcal B(Vy,Vx)$ and edges joining $\bar b b$ to $1_{Vx}$ in $\mathcal B(Vx,Vx)$ and $b\bar b$ to $1_{Vy}$ in $\mathcal B(Vy,Vy)$. In a Kan complex edges can be reversed (fill $\Lambda^2_0$) and concatenated (fill $\Lambda^2_1$), so orientation is immaterial. Let $(a,\gamma)$ be a point of $\mathcal N_V(x,y;b)$, $\gamma$ an edge from $V(a)$ to $b$. By Step 1, $\mathcal N_V(y,x;\bar b)$ is nonempty: choose $(c,\delta)$, $\delta$ from $V(c)$ to $\bar b$. Step 2 gives an edge $\delta\gamma$ from $V(ca)=V(c)V(a)$ to $\bar b b$; concatenating it in the Kan complex $\mathcal B(Vx,Vx)$ with the edge to $1_{Vx}$ gives a point $(ca,\epsilon)$ of $\mathcal N_V(x,x;1_{Vx})$. Since $V$ preserves identities, $(1_x,\operatorname{const}_{1_{Vx}})$ is another point. By Step 1 this fibre is contractible, so its realization is path connected; path components of a realization are the classes of vertices under the equivalence relation generated by edges, so the two points are joined by a zigzag of edges. Projecting to $\mathcal A(x,x)$ gives a zigzag from $ca$ to $1_x$, which the Kan property of $\mathcal A(x,x)$ turns into a single homotopy $ca\simeq1_x$. The same argument in $\mathcal N_V(y,y;1_{Vy})$, using $b\bar b\simeq1_{Vy}$, gives $ac\simeq1_y$. Thus every corresponding $a$ is invertible up to enriched homotopy.

proof.text: For an enriched homotopy equivalence $f:x\to y$, choose an inverse $g:y\to x$ and edges $H$ from $gf$ to $1_x$ in $\mathcal A(x,x)$ and $K$ from $fg$ to $1_y$ in $\mathcal A(y,y)$. Precomposition with $f$ is the simplicial map $r:\mathcal A(y,x)\to\mathcal A(x,x)$, $h\mapsto h\circ f$, and $s:\mathcal A(x,x)\to\mathcal A(y,x)$ is $k\mapsto k\circ g$. The composites $\mathcal A(x,x)\times\Delta^1\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\times H}\mathcal A(x,x)\times\mathcal A(x,x)\xrightarrow{\circ}\mathcal A(x,x)$ and $\mathcal A(y,x)\times\Delta^1\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\times K}\mathcal A(y,x)\times\mathcal A(y,y)\xrightarrow{\circ}\mathcal A(y,x)$ are simplicial homotopies from $rs$ to $\mathrm{id}$ and from $sr$ to $\mathrm{id}$, by associativity and the unit law. The general simplicial-homotopy-equivalence lemma [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] therefore makes $r$ a weak homotopy equivalence between Kan complexes (locally Kan). Applying [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] to $r$ over $1_x$ shows its homotopy fibre is contractible. A point is exactly an $h\in\mathcal A(y,x)$ with an edge from $hf$ to $1_x$; $(g,H)$ is one. As in Step 3, contractibility joins $(h,\cdot)$ and $(g,H)$ by a zigzag of edges whose projection gives $h\simeq g$ in the Kan complex $\mathcal A(y,x)$. Postcomposition with $f$, the simplicial map $\mathcal A(y,x)\to\mathcal A(y,y)$, carries it to $fh\simeq fg$, and concatenation with $K$ gives the second homotopy $fh\simeq1_y$.
